newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak cen bank says not to hike repo rate yet.
newsitem.headline: Slovak cen bank says not to hike repo rate yet.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) on Wednesday said it would not hike its repo rate, currently 9.7 percent, despite a further rise in the average yield at the Finance Ministry's 39-week T-bill auction.

"We will not react to the T-bill yield increase (to 9.998 percent from 9.669 percent) yet, as it seems unneccessary due to the minor volume drained in the auction," Peter Andresic, NBS chief dealer, told Reuters. "However, such a yield increase is not good."

Earlier on Wednesday, average yield at an auction of the ministry 39-week T-bills was 9.986 percent, up from 9.669 percent in the last auction of similar bills. The market expected that to bring about an increase in the repo rate.
Only 209 million crowns worth of bids from a total of 1.089 billion crowns were accepted, but the ministry's borrowing needs were larlely covered by the NBS itself..

"By taking one billion crowns worth of T-bills into its (the central bank's) portfolio before the auction, the NBS did not expose the ministry to the need to obtain the needed funds from the market," Andresic added.

Andresic added that with some seven billion crowns worth of bills maturing on the market next week, an influx of liquidity "will be rather difficult to handle" and the NBS may have to raise the repo rate.
